<reason>B won by distinguishing mandatory pre-release evaluation from discretionary approval and answering pressure with an enforceable testing duty and a concrete withholding trigger. A established a serious concern about irreversible releases and future adaptation, but repeatedly treated incomplete testing as sufficient justification for reversing the default without adequately defending its alternative standard. B exposed that affirmative approval would face the same epistemic limits and explained why capability criteria need not enumerate every attack. A’s final speech largely repeated irreversibility rather than resolving that comparison or explaining when advanced openness could actually qualify for approval.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest rebuttal was that A’s approval regime still relies on the hostile testing A calls inadequate. Combined with the distinction between permanence and demonstrated danger, this forced A to defend an achievable approval standard rather than merely reiterate the consequences of a false negative.</best_rebuttal>
